The Trump administration unveiled a national AI framework that allocates proper regulatory authority between the federal government and states while also maintaining a light-touch approach, writes Cato's @kevintfrazier. 
ow.ly/A53l50YxPhp

The Pentagon’s new Economic Defense Unit is reportedly recruiting Wall Street talent from firms tied to the industries it may target. Cato’s @DeHavenTad warns this looks less like defense policy and more like a shadow investment fund.
ow.ly/bsos50YxP7A

A 30-day DHS shutdown hasn’t slowed ICE or Border Patrol—nearly $170 billion in funding keeps them running with minimal transparency and oversight. On the latest Cato Podcast, @LettDominik and @David_J_Bier break down what this reveals about Washington’s broken appropriations process. 

Apple Podcasts: ow.ly/fWG350YxHiS
Spotify: ow.ly/MmJ750YxHiR
Website: ow.ly/8soB50YxHiQ

F.A. Hayek (1899-1992), one of the most important free market economists in history, died on March 23, 1992. 

He refuted the tenets of socialism in his best-selling book “The Road to Serfdom,” and was awarded the Nobel Prize in Economics in 1974. If you want to fight for freedom, study Hayek.

Trump’s rationales for denying birthright citizenship to children of undocumented immigrants are at odds with the 14th Amendment’s core purpose: granting citizenship to freed slaves and their descendants. The original meaning counts against the administration, reports Cato’s @IlyaSomin. 
ow.ly/Svn850YxIvf

Wearable technology promises unprecedented insight into our bodies, but they are rapidly becoming the backbone of a new surveillance infrastructure, warns Cato’s @dr4liberty.

Video

Republicans keep expanding farm subsidies—$23 billion in 2025 rising to $42 billion by 2027—and most of it goes to wealthy farms. Meanwhile, Republicans claim they oppose wasteful spending and debt. This is not “fiscal conservatism.” It’s farm welfare, explains Cato’s @CatoEdwards. 

ow.ly/ONSR50YxMMF

The Cato Institute’s @cpgrabow discussed the Jones Act and US shipbuilding with @LesleyRStahl on CBS’s @60Minutes. 

Watch full segment: piped.video/fj0tE2wwTVM?si=Lscj…

Video

Sweeping AI bills could risk stunting US innovation by smothering entrepreneurs with heavy-handed regulation at the very moment America needs a light-touch approach, explains Cato’s @KevinTFrazier  and @jrhuddles.  

ow.ly/QWz650YxH7v

Our national debt is a spending problem, not a revenue problem, says Cato’s @adamnmichel. History shows that raising taxes won’t fix the deficit—controlling government spending will. 

ow.ly/pezX50YxCRT

Join the Cato Institute for a policy discussion on Section 122 of the Trade Act of 1974 and congressional tariff authorities. 

Featuring Cato’s @clark_packard, Representative @RepJimmyPanetta (D CA), @stanveuger of the American Enterprise Institute, and Former Chief of Staff for Representative Ron Kind (D WI), @hana_leah. 
  
🗓️ March 26 | 3 PM EDT 
📍 Cato Institute

Immigrants are making us more productive and wealthier—and ultimately, that results in more tax payments, says the Cato Institute’s @David_J_Bier. He discussed immigration on “Why Is This Happening?” podcast with @chrislhayes. 

➡️ ow.ly/YUMk50YwWS1

Video

As federal debt continues to rise, taxpayers are footing billions each year for farm subsidies that primarily benefit large agribusinesses and insurance companies. Businesses in other industries manage their own risks to stay afloat in competitive markets, and so should farm businesses. 

ow.ly/730n50Yx2yK

Government policies, not greedy developers or investors, are a major factor in the decline of the American starter home, reports Cato’s @scottlincicome.

Section 230 really became the 26 words that created the internet, says Samir Jain, VP of Policy at the Center for Democracy & Technology. 

Watch Cato Institute’s discussion on the past, present, and future of online speech and Section 230: piped.video/live/ZB1-S8UWtMo

Video

Pakistan’s @dawn_com applauds "No Compulsion in Religion—No Exceptions", edited by Cato’s @AkyolinEnglish. The book argues the Quran’s “no compulsion in religion” applies universally, challenging all religious coercion. It shows freedom is rooted in Islamic tradition—not a Western import.
